S01: Brunhilde was a valkyrie — a warrior who served Odin.
S02: She was the bravest among them.
S03: The valkyries led the fallen warriors to Odin's hall.
S04: But once, Brunhilde disobeyed one of Odin's commands.
S06: As punishment, he turned her into a mortal maiden and locked her in a castle.
S07: Odin: "You shall remain here until a knight comes to free you!"
S08: A thousand shields rose around the castle.
S09: And around it a ring of fire blazed.
S10: With ancient magic, Odin cast her into a deep sleep.
S11: Brunhilde closed her eyes and slept.
S12: And meanwhile, the young Sigurd was already riding toward the castle.
S13: Sigurd followed the voice of the birds.
S14: He knew the birds led him toward destiny.
S15: At last before him appeared the enchanted castle.
S16: Before him rose a thousand shields.
S17: He was so brave that nothing frightened him.
S19: The shields parted before the pure heart.
S20: The thousand shields opened a path for him.
S23: He walked through the fire unharmed.
S24: The fire did not touch the brave young man.
S25: In the heart of the castle, a maiden lay sleeping.
S26: She was beautiful as a dream.
S28: Then, the maiden opened her eyes.
S30: Sigurd fell in love with her at first sight.
S31: And he gave her the magic ring from the dragon Fafnir.
S32: He placed it on her finger.
S33: The curse of Odin was broken.
S34: The ring of fire went out, and the shields grew still.
S35: Sigurd: "I give you my sword: I shall protect you and love you forever."
S36: And Brunhilde, free, accepted him with all her heart.
S37: The two walked out of the castle toward the first light.
S38: The ring of fire was now only a garland of embers.
S39: The shields lay like sleeping warriors.
S40: The faithful horse awaited its master.
S41: They rode together across the fields.
S42: She was now mortal — but freer than ever.
S43: The birds led them along the road toward the new day.
S44: Brunhilde: "You have returned my heart to me, Sigurd."
S45: The ring of Fafnir gleamed like a small star.
S48: From that day, Sigurd and Brunhilde were inseparable — shielded by a love stronger than any fire.
